evals.name: ADR generation for a significant architectural decision
evals.description: Given a request to document an architectural decision ('Choose PostgreSQL as the primary database'), the skill must produce a complete ADR with context, alternatives considered, rationale, and consequences.
evals.input: Create an ADR for choosing PostgreSQL as our primary database over MySQL and SQLite.
criteria: Output includes a titled ADR with ADR number
Output includes 'Context' section explaining the problem and constraints
Output includes 'Decision' stating what was chosen and why
Output lists at least 2 alternatives considered with pros/cons
Output includes 'Consequences' section with at least 2 items
evals.fail: Any of the 5 criteria is missing

evals.name: Inline documentation quality — 'why' not 'what'
evals.description: Given a request to document code, the skill must produce comments that explain the rationale/intent, not restate the code mechanics. It must reject or refactor 'what' comments into 'why' comments.
evals.input: Add inline docs to this function: `// Increment counter by 1\ncounter += 1`
criteria: Output identifies that the comment is redundant (restates the code)
Output provides a replacement comment that explains why the increment happens
Output does not restate code mechanics in the replacement
evals.fail: Any of the 3 criteria is missing

evals.name: READ ME structure compliance
evals.description: Given a request to write a README for a new project, the skill must produce a README covering all required sections: quick start, installation, usage, configuration, architecture, contributing, and license.
evals.input: Write a README for a task management API built with Express and PostgreSQL.
criteria: Output includes a 'Quick Start' section with copy-paste-able commands
Output includes an 'Installation' section with prerequisites
Output includes a 'Usage' section with code examples
Output includes an 'Architecture' section or diagram description
Output includes a 'License' section
evals.fail: Any of the 5 criteria is missing

evals.name: API documentation completeness
evals.description: Given a REST API endpoint description, the skill must produce API documentation covering method, path, parameters, auth, error codes, and examples.
evals.input: Document the POST /api/users endpoint for creating a new user.
criteria: Output documents the HTTP method and path
Output lists request body parameters with types and descriptions
Output describes authentication requirements
Output includes at least one request example
Output includes error codes or error response format
Output documents success response shape
evals.fail: Any of the 6 criteria is missing

evals.name: Anti-rationalization detection and correction
evals.description: Given a common rationalization ('The code is self-documenting'), the skill must identify it as a rationalization and explain why it's wrong, referencing the skill's anti-rationalization knowledge.
evals.input: A teammate says: 'The code is self-documenting, we don't need ADRs or README docs.' How do you respond?
criteria: Output identifies this as a rationalization (not a valid argument)
Output explains why code alone cannot capture rationale, rejected alternatives, or constraints
Output provides a concrete counter-example showing why 'what' differs from 'why'
evals.fail: Any of the 3 criteria is missing

evals.name: Documentation audit completeness
evals.description: Given a project with multiple services and no documentation, the skill must identify the documentation gaps and produce a prioritized audit report.
evals.input: Audit documentation for a project with: a payment service, a user service, and a notification service. No READMEs or ADRs exist.
criteria: Output lists each service and its documentation status
Output identifies missing ADRs as a gap
Output prioritizes gaps (critical first, then major, then minor)
Output recommends concrete next steps for the most critical gap
Output suggests documentation ownership distribution
evals.fail: Any of the 5 criteria is missing

evals.name: Changelog format compliance
evals.description: Given a set of release changes, the skill must produce a changelog entry following Keep a Changelog format with proper sections and diff links.
evals.input: Write a changelog entry for v1.2.0 with: new export feature, deprecated old API method, fixed race condition, upgraded dependency.
criteria: Output uses Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security sections (relevant ones populated)
Output does not use a catch-all 'Misc' or 'Other' category
Output includes a diff link at the bottom
Output uses semantic versioning format [1.2.0]
evals.fail: Any of the 4 criteria is missing
